correctness.rationale: The graph is defined intrinsically as GP(10,2). Exhaustive enumeration checks 5,828 faces (including the empty face) with nonempty cardinality counts 20,160,660,1510,1912,1240,320,5. The deterministic matching has 2,911 cover pairs and exactly one critical 0-cell plus four critical 5-cells. The full 27,620-edge oriented Hasse diagram is topologically sorted, certifying acyclicity. Discrete Morse theory then gives a CW model with one 0-cell and four 5-cells, hence \(\bigvee^4 S^5\).

A second full-text comparison, Goyal--Shukla--Singh arXiv:1905.06926, proves wedge decompositions for different graph families and likewise contains no dodecahedral/Petersen-family statement. Targeted alias searches and semantic-database searches found no equivalent or stronger statement. Search failure is not treated as proof of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: A full homotopy type for a canonical 20-vertex cubic symmetric/Platonic graph is a natural exact datum, not an arbitrary slice. Berghoff’s nearby Petersen and cube examples make standard cubic graphs a motivated testing ground, while the explicit wedge \(\bigvee^4S^5\) compresses a 5,828-face complex to five critical cells. The result is a reproducible benchmark for methods studying independence-complex topology.
